verdict.rationale: Crossplane documents composition functions that let you write configuration in general-purpose languages such as Python and Go, plus KCL. These functions return the declarative configuration Crossplane applies, so infrastructure logic can be expressed in real code. However, this sits inside a YAML/Kubernetes composition pipeline rather than being a full code-first IaC model, and the evidence never mentions types, loops or IDE support. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of typed SDKs, loops/abstractions in function code, IDE tooling or autocomplete, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define infrastructure in a general-purpose programming language with types, loops, and IDE support

citations.quote: Functions allow you to write your configuration in multiple languages, including YAML, KCL, Python, and Go.
The functions return declarative configuration that Crossplane should apply.
Functions extend Crossplane with new ways to configure composition
